Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Key ask from Acme: DPA and confirmation of which SCC module(s) you want Redwood to sign.
- From our discussion it sounded like Acme will be the Data Controller and Redwood will act as a Processor for the hosted inference integration. Please confirm if that is correct.
- I've attached a short checklist ("SCC_Modular_Options.xlsx") with the typical choices we see and a draft DPA template we normally use.

Action items:
1) Sophie/Acme: confirm Controller vs Processor roles and whether you want the EU Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses in the Controller-Processor configuration (Module II under the legacy nomenclature / Controller-Processor under the 2021 SCC framework).
2) Acme legal: if you prefer to use your standard DPA, please send over the PDF (we can review redlines).
3) Rishi/Neha (internal): once Sophie confirms, we’ll propose the final SCC selection and route the DPA to legal for signature.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Request_20270304.pdf (your questionnaire), SCC_Modular_Options.xlsx

Happy to hop on a short call with legal if that helps.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Acme GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection

Thanks Marissa —

Confirming: Acme will be the Data Controller for our customer data; Redwood will be the Processor.

A few clarifying Qs:
- Can Redwood execute Acme's standard DPA or do you require us to sign Redwood's template? We generally prefer to use our boilerplate but can be flexible.
- For SCCs: we expect controller -> processor flow. If you could recommend the exact SCC text (2021 SCCs) and highlight any deviations, that would speed review.
- Timeline: we'd like an initial DPA + SCC proposal within 1 week if possible — legal will prioritize once we have a draft.

Sophie Turner
Director, Integrations | Acme Corp
sophie.turner@acme.com

Sophie —

Thanks for the quick confirmation on roles. I've attached a draft DPA (Redwood_Draft_DPA_20270305.pdf) and a short guidance note in the SCC spreadsheet recommending the Controller-Processor variant of the 2021 SCCs (we've labeled it "Controller->Processor / Module II (2021 SCC)" in the XLSX). In practice that's the typical configuration for SaaS vendors where the customer is the controller and the vendor is the processor.

Highlights / caveats:
- Redwood's standard DPA aligns with the 2021 SCCs; we generally accept reasonable customer redlines but we do need legal review for any substantive changes to security or subprocessors clauses.
- If Acme wants to use your boilerplate DPA, please send it and we'll loop in our counsel.
- Proposed timeline: we can deliver a signed DPA within ~10 business days assuming only minor redlines; if Acme requires contract review cycles longer than that, please flag.

Next steps:
- Sophie/Acme legal: confirm whether you'll use your DPA or Redwood's draft. If yours, please attach.
- Acme: confirm you accept Controller->Processor SCC configuration (we recommend this).
- Rishi/Neha: I'll prepare the internal legal intake and assign to our counsel once Sophie confirms.

Attachments: Redwood_Draft_DPA_20270305.pdf, SCC_Modular_Options.xlsx

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Sophie / Acme legal —

Following up to confirm Redwood's position and next steps:

- Role alignment: Redwood will act as Processor; Acme will be Controller.
- SCC selection: we agree Controller->Processor (2021 SCCs) for cross-border data transfer coverage. Please confirm you want the standard Controller->Processor clauses; we'll include them in the DPA.
- DPA execution: Marissa attached our draft DPA; we can also accept your DPA for review. For speed, I recommend we proceed with our draft and handle any Acme redlines — this usually shortens turnaround.

Proposed timeline and steps:
1) Sophie/legal: confirm SCC Module = Controller->Processor (reply to this thread).
2) If Acme wants to use its DPA, upload to the HubSpot deal or send PDF to legal@redwood.com. Otherwise we will send the DocuSign packet using the link below.
3) Once DPA/SCC agreed, we'll move to signature. Target: executed DPA within 10 business days.
